questions.topic: Bonding in Carbon – the Covalent Bond
questions.stem:
A student is explaining to the class how the two atoms are joined together in a nitrogen molecule, N2.
Assertion 1: In N2, each nitrogen atom shares three electrons with the other, so three shared pairs of electrons are formed.
Reason 1: Nitrogen has the atomic number 7, and in order to attain an octet each nitrogen atom contributes three electrons. (A) Both Assertion 1 and Reason 1 are true and Reason 1 is the correct explanation of Assertion 1. (B) Both Assertion 1 and Reason 1 are true but Reason 1 is not the correct explanation of Assertion 1. (C) Assertion 1 is true but Reason 1 is false. (D) Both Assertion 1 and Reason 1 are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both Assertion 1 and Reason 1 are true and Reason 1 is the correct explanation of Assertion 1.

questions.stem:
Two hydrogen atoms join up to form a molecule of hydrogen, H2. A student wants to know how the two atoms are held together.
Assertion 1: The two hydrogen atoms in a molecule of hydrogen are joined by a single covalent bond.
Reason 1: Each hydrogen atom has one electron in its K shell and so must gain two more electrons to attain the electronic configuration of helium. (A) Both Assertion 1 and Reason 1 are true and Reason 1 is the correct explanation of Assertion 1. (B) Both Assertion 1 and Reason 1 are true but Reason 1 is not the correct explanation of Assertion 1. (C) Assertion 1 is true but Reason 1 is false. (D) Both Assertion 1 and Reason 1 are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Assertion 1 is true but Reason 1 is false.

questions.stem:
A student is asked whether carbon forms ionic compounds by gaining or losing its outermost electrons.
Assertion 1: A carbon atom forms a compound by losing its four outermost electrons, leaving a carbon cation with six protons in its nucleus holding on to just two electrons.
Reason 1: Only a small amount of energy is needed to remove four electrons from a carbon atom. (A) Both Assertion 1 and Reason 1 are true and Reason 1 is the correct explanation of Assertion 1. (B) Both Assertion 1 and Reason 1 are true but Reason 1 is not the correct explanation of Assertion 1. (C) Assertion 1 is true but Reason 1 is false. (D) Both Assertion 1 and Reason 1 are false.
